title: How an Air Conditioner Works in 60 Seconds ❄️🏠 #shorts
description:
An air conditioner doesn't create cold. It moves heat. A refrigerant evaporates in the indoor coil and soaks up heat from your room, a compressor squeezes it hot, the outdoor coil dumps that heat outside, and an expansion valve chills it again. Absorb, squeeze, release, repeat. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#airconditioner #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Secret
steps.text: An air conditioner doesn't make cold. It *moves heat* from inside your home to the outside.

steps.label: Evaporator
steps.text: Indoors, cold *refrigerant* flows through a coil. It soaks up heat from your room and turns into a gas.

steps.label: Compressor
steps.text: Outside, a *compressor* squeezes that gas, making it very hot and high pressure.

steps.label: Condenser
steps.text: A fan blows across the outdoor coil, dumping the *heat* outside. The gas turns back into liquid.

steps.label: Expansion Valve
steps.text: A tiny *valve* drops the pressure, and the refrigerant becomes ice cold again.

steps.label: Dripping Water
steps.text: The cold coil also pulls *moisture* from the air. That's why AC units drip.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Absorb, squeeze, release, *repeat*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
